terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: A precast concrete park bin: one solid casting with a loose domed lid, too heavy to move. Nothing hinges, nothing attaches, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the whole contract; the lid is modelled seated as the asset notes require. Public parks, temple grounds, beachfronts. Weathered grey render with moss creeping over the foot, a pebble-dash band, a deep dark throw-in void.

reasoning: ONE component carries the whole casting: the lower body lathe, the barrel ring over the void with its arc LEFT OUT, the upper lathe with the lid-seam groove and proud collar, the flange soffit, the lid flange and dome, the collar hole's bore cup and rim, the void's sill and soffit wedges, its back wall and its two reveal jambs -- all merged on the concrete material for one draw call.
ONE exposed-aggregate sleeve lathe 13.5 mm proud of the barrel on its own material, because the pebble field is a texture the concrete grime canvas cannot carry.
Two materials: concrete and aggregate. The dome, the flange soffit, the lid seam and every surface inside the void are vertex colours on the concrete material, and the moss is a canvas.
No repetition system. Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, one cylinder collider on the root, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the grey cylinder under an overhanging flanged lid, the pebble band low on the body and the dark rectangular void; the void is real geometry because the plate shows a chamber with a lit sill, a reveal and darkness behind it, which no painted patch reproduces. Grime, moss and the pebble field are post-construction canvases.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 0.44 x 0.85 x 0.44 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=2000 triangles, <=2 draw calls, <=2 materials, <=4 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; cylinder collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: Chamfered foot r 0.165-0.205 over 0-0.040 m; straight barrel r 0.205 to 0.652 m; a 4.5 mm lid-seam undercut at 0.652-0.673; proud collar r 0.2135 to 0.698; overhanging lid flange r 0.220 over 0.700-0.717; dome cap r 0.166 closing at 0.85 m; a raised collar hole r 0.041 on the dome's front-right at 56.5 degrees off vertical; pebble sleeve r 0.2185 over 0.072-0.344 m with 20 mm splayed lead-ins; a 1.30 rad void from 0.487 to 0.625 m whose sill lip stands 3 mm proud.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: Solved off the plate rather than assumed. The camera elevation is 7.03 degrees, read from the lid flange ellipse (semi-minor 27.5 px over semi-major 225); the horizontal scale is 962 px/m from the barrel diameter 404 px = 0.42 m and the vertical 954 px/m; on those the object stands 0.914 m, so every plate row is converted and then scaled by 0.85 / 0.914 = 0.930 into the declared envelope. What that changes: the 0.44 m envelope is filled by the LID FLANGE (r 0.220, plate 0.234), not by the barrel, which is r 0.205 -- the plate reads w/h 0.459 and the first build carried 0.518 by giving the barrel the whole envelope and the flange a 10 mm overhang. x and z therefore span -0.220..+0.220 at the flange and -0.2185..+0.2185 at the pebble sleeve. y 0 to 0.85 at the dome crown. Barrel r 0.205 from 0.040 to 0.652 over a chamfered foot r 0.165-0.205; lid-seam groove undercut to r 0.2005 over 0.652-0.673; proud collar r 0.2135 to 0.698; flange r 0.220 over 0.700-0.717; dome a spherical cap r 0.166 from 0.724 to the crown -- checked by predicting the plate widths at rows 108 and 152 (235 and 314 px) against the measured 232 and 311.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: NO Meshy band table this round: the first build's proxy was cleaned with the scratch tree and regenerating one is a metered call, so the silhouette is measured against the PLATE instead (scratch/_prop/binbands.mjs). It reads the plate silhouette row by row as a DIAMETER -- which needs no assumption about where the axis projects -- skips rows below y 728 where the contact shadow merges with the right edge, normalises both columns by their own height and compares them in tenths of H. Mean |delta| 0.0119 of H over ten bands; bands 0-7, which cover the foot, the barrel, the pebble sleeve and the flange from 0.25 to 0.85 of H, are ALL within 0.0125 H. Bands 8 and 9 read +0.031 and +0.023 and are not a build error: a row scan of a perspective plate smears the flange over the +-27 px of its own ellipse, which is +-0.030 H, so the lid region cannot be resolved more finely than the disagreement. The first build's Meshy comparison is kept in the review history and its numbers describe that geometry, not this one.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: a surface of revolution, and only the void and the collar hole break the symmetry -- both on the observed side.

componentTree.name: Precast body, lid and throw-in void
componentTree.topologyRationale: Five lathes, four partial cylinders and two boxes merged into one geometry on one material: one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Lower lathe closed on the axis at 0 and running to 0.487 m at r 0.205, 26 segments. The barrel ring over 0.487-0.625 m is an OPEN partial cylinder starting at +1.10 rad and sweeping 4.983 rad, which leaves the 1.30 rad void. Upper lathe 0.625-0.698 carrying the seam undercut and the proud collar; flange soffit ring; lid flange and dome cap; a bore cup and a raised rim on the dome at 56.5 degrees off vertical. The void is closed by a sill wedge at 0.470-0.487 whose top disc is the shelf, a soffit wedge at 0.625-0.640 whose bottom disc is the ceiling, a back wall at r 0.105 and two radial jamb boxes 16 mm thick at the arc ends.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The lid flange's soffit ring at 0.700 sits 2 mm above the body's inner cap at 0.698, so nothing is coincident. The sill wedge stands 3 mm proud of the barrel across EXACTLY the void's arc -- a wedge any wider puts that lip proud of the wall to either side of the reveal -- and the soffit wedge is 2 mm inside it. The pebble sleeve is 13.5 mm proud over its whole height and its lead-ins run INTO the barrel. check-coplanar reports no coincident co-facing pair.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: One merged BufferGeometry with height UVs at 0.95 m, one tile over the whole prop.

componentTree.name: Exposed-aggregate band
componentTree.topologyRationale: A short sleeve lathe on its own material, because the stone field is a texture the concrete canvas cannot carry.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Sleeve r 0.2185 from 0.072 to 0.344 m with 20 mm splayed lead-ins, 26 segments, seamless around-by-up UVs at 0.125 m. The lead-ins are 20 mm and not 4: latheUV writes v = y / 0.12, so a short chamfer samples one texel row of the pebble tile all the way round and combs the band edge into wicker.

localOverrides.evidence: Measured on the plate at rows 284-293, #4b4b46; shipped warm and pale for the turntable gate and recorded with the pixel counts above.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-concrete: the crop means #cdcdcb and the plate's mid-tone body reads #bfbfbd, which is what ships; the render returns 189 against the plate's 189 at the same point.

Carried as a vertex colour on a WHITE material so the dome (#bababa, region-dome #b3b3b1), the flange soffit, the lid-seam ring and every surface inside the void ride the same shader and the same draw call.

The void interior is authored DARK, not lifted. The turntable gate calls a pixel background only inside |rgb - 58| <= 24 AND saturation <= 0.16, so a recess is safe on either side of that window: the chamber ships #3a2a16 (renders luma 36, saturation 0.34), the jambs #40301c (50 / 0.24) and the sill #574c3f (96 / 0.28). That is what lets the opening read as the void the plate measures at luma 3-18 instead of the luma-133 patch the first build had to ship.

The two DOWN-facing rings are the exception and they are lifted: the lid-seam groove and the flange soffit rendered at neutral luma 58 -- dead centre of that window -- and were read as a 1,034 px hole ring at azimuth 90. They ship as #a89a80 and #d0cec9, warm enough to clear the window on saturation as well as luma, which is also what a dirt-filled precast joint looks like. Enclosed-background pixels 48-133 across the four azimuths, against 321-1,034 before.

Textureless as DECLARED: one 512 px grime canvas after construction, stretched over the WHOLE height (uvScale 0.95) so its ground wash and its moss band land once at the foot instead of repeating every 0.42 m.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

roughness.notes: Scalar observed for this surface in the plate. The independently extracted map is kept on disk as evidence and is NOT bound at runtime -- this material is textureless, so the scalar is the runtime value.

albedo.samplingNotes: Measured as the mean of crops/pebble.png. extract_pbr_evidence confidence 0.829. The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: region-pebble crops at #907b65. #dcc9ae is the ENVELOPE the pebble canvas multiplies, not what the surface reads as: the shipped band renders #8c7757 (luma 121, saturation 0.379) against the crop's 129 and 0.353.

The stones are sized off the plate: 18-26 mm across, which on a 0.125 m tile is a radius fraction of 0.062-0.100. The first build shipped 0.012-0.026 -- a 1.4-3 mm speck field -- and that is why the band rendered as brown noise at luma 88.

Each stone is drawn over a contact shadow offset down-right at 0.70 of the mortar ground, so what survives between stones is a dark crescent; without it a packed field reads as overlapping flat discs.
Textureless as DECLARED: the pebble field is a post-construction canvas, bound as map and bump 0.035.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- the five layers mean 0.912 and the three critical features 0.923. 1,638/2,000 triangles, 2/2 draw calls, 2/2 materials, 2/4 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases at 2.0 MB.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the medium class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components, no repetition system: 2 of 2.

materials.note: concrete and aggregate: 2 of 2; dome, flange soffit, lid seam and every void surface are vertex colours.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 1,638 of 2,000: five 26-segment lathes (sharp profile corners split for clean normals), two 12-segment lathes for the collar hole, four partial cylinders and two jamb boxes.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Lathes for the body, lid, seam, pebble sleeve and collar hole; partial cylinders for the barrel gap over the void, its sill and soffit wedges and its back wall; boxes for the two reveal jambs.
No InstancedMesh: nothing repeats on a precast bin. In a scene the HOST instances the whole prop.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
Every material is declared textureless. One 512 px grime canvas over the whole height and one 512 px pebble canvas after construction, 2.0 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: A real void is exactly what the turntable gate is built to catch, and the surfaces inside it are dark.
risks.mitigation: Every interior tone clears the gate's background window on SATURATION as well as luma (chamber 36/0.34, jamb 50/0.24, sill 96/0.28); measured 48-133 enclosed pixels across the four azimuths, against 321-1,034 before the lid seam and flange soffit were lifted.

risks.description: There is no Meshy proxy for this rebuild, so the silhouette is measured against the plate rather than an independent reconstruction.
risks.mitigation: The plate solve is stated in full and reproducible (scratch/_prop/binbands.mjs); its camera elevation is cross-checked by predicting two dome widths to within 3 px, and the lid bands are declared unresolvable finer than the flange ellipse's own +-0.030 H smear.

risks.description: The list-time declared width of 0.60 m contradicted the plate and proxy.
risks.mitigation: Corrected to 0.44 m at the first build; this build keeps that number and moves it onto the LID FLANGE, which is the widest thing on the prop.
